paragraphs: OKhuman sells a writing provenance tool that a student installs and uses to create a stamp on work written in any application. The stamp is offered as evidence of effort rather than as an inspection of the finished text for machine authorship. The pages state that this works in any writing app and without recording the words themselves.

The home page speaks to students, faculty, institutions and admissions officers. For faculty, the stated use is to see whether a student put effort into an assignment and then grade the writing itself. For institutions, the pages tie the stamp to written assignments and to what a credential is meant to signal about a graduate. For admissions readers, the stamp is described as a way to weigh effort separately from the quality of an essay.

The about page frames the product as infrastructure that makes the writing process verifiable, set against detection that inspects output. The team listed there is described as bringing experience in content protection, high scale systems, and scientific research.

quote.text: OKhuman lets you show proof of your effort.
